title: Unified Entryways: Workspace Palette & Lightweight Routing Proposal
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Proposal for a lightweight, incremental redesign of the Redwood Console information architecture focused on: 1) a ‘Workspace Palette’ as a low-friction global entrypoint for workspace switching and task jump-ins, 2) a simplified left rail that surfaces user journeys (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Lens, Models) as contextual entryways rather than deep nested folders, and 3) route anchors and progressive disclosure to reduce cognitive load and improve first-time discovery. Goals: reduce average workspace switch time by 40%, decrease lateral navigation clicks for common tasks, and surface cost/rollout signals earlier in the workflow. Constraints: must be compatible with Dedicated/Private feature flags, minimal backend route churn, accessible keyboard-first interactions, and preserve existing telemetry for cost and latency metrics.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Sofia Patel: initial brief uploaded. Scope includes a new Workspace Palette modal, reduced left-rail density, and per-route micro-entries for cost & rollout quick-actions. Refer to PRD (link in attachments).

2025-02-16 - Ethan Liu: added low-fidelity flows and keyboard interactions. Raised question about whether Workspace Palette should be modal or anchored panel — leaning modal to avoid persistent state conflicts with Dedicated layout.
2025-02-19 - Miguel Torres (PM): asked for compatibility checklist for Private (VPC) where certain routes are hidden by policy. Added ENG dependency to gate route-level flags.

2025-02-24 - Design critique: recommended merging 'Cost Lens' card into primary dashboard entry for faster discoverability and showing a cost delta badge on workspace tiles. Decision: show small cost delta tag on workspace palette items; open details still live in Cost view.

2025-02-28 - UX Research: guerrilla testing (n=12) on low-fi prototype. Findings: users discovered workspace switcher faster when palette uses fuzzy search + recent pins; some confusion when rollouts actions are nested under models. Action: surface 2 primary quick-actions (Open Rollouts, Open Cost) on hover in palette.

2025-03-03 - Engineering review (ENG-27821): backend route anchors accepted, but requested stable route names for telemetry. Added requirement: new route aliases to map to existing telemetry tags to avoid losing historical dashboards.
2025-03-04 - Sofia Patel: updated prototype to reflect engineering feedback; preparing handed-off spec for front-end engineers and accessibility checklist. Planning handoff meeting 2025-03-06.
Follow-ups: analytics experiment to measure workspace switch time, A/B test for palette modal vs anchored panel, and perf budget for route bundle size.
